issues.title: Missing trace in the Fair-SMW reformulated objective
issues.failure_explanation: The paper specifies H in R^{n×k}, so H^T G(I-F(F^TGF)^{-1}F^TG)H is k-by-k. Although it is scalar when k=1, the claimed and experimental regime includes k>1, where no scalar maximum or matrix ordering is specified. Equations SMW1 and SMW3b use a trace objective, and the text says the displayed reformulation is obtained from SMW3b, so the omitted trace is uniquely forced by the old source.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the labeled final reformulation does not define the advertised scalar variational problem for multicluster embeddings. The intended objective and eigenvector construction remain recoverable from the immediately preceding trace formulation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing trace, so the reformulation reads max over H^T H = I of Tr[H^T G(I-F(F^TGF)^{-1}F^TG)H]. No proof or algorithmic change is needed.
issues.why_classification: For k>1 the displayed expression is matrix-valued, while SMW1 and SMW3b are explicitly trace objectives and the text says the reformulation follows from SMW3b. The old source therefore uniquely forces the omitted trace, and restoring it repairs only transcription, not any mathematical inference.

issues.title: False general real-spectrum guarantee for the random-walk construction

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The expression $F^T D^{-1} = F^T D^{-1} P_F$ holds true if and only if every row vector of $F^T D^{-1}$ is invariant under the projection $P_F$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof needs the identity F^T D^{-1}=F^T D^{-1}F(F^T F)^{-1}F^T. Invertibility of D^{-1} preserves rank, not the particular row space of F^T, and therefore does not imply invariance under P_F. For the admissible two-group choice F=(1,-1/3,-1/3,-1/3)^T and symmetric weights (w12,w13,w14,w23,w24,w34)=(13,1,36,3,9,1), one has D=diag(50,25,5,46) and F^T G_rw F=3448/1725, so all required inverses exist, but U_rw has a conjugate pair approximately 1.6976±0.0567i. Thus the unconditional theorem itself is false.
issues.overall_effect: The random-walk Fair-SMW variant lacks the claimed theoretical basis for treating U_rw as a real-spectrum operator and obtaining an always-real top-k embedding on general irregular graphs. The symmetric-variant theorem is unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retract the unconditional real-spectrum theorem and its proof, state explicitly that U_rw may have complex eigenvalues on admissible irregular graphs, and remove every general always-real top-k claim for RW-Fair-SMW. To retain an executable real-valued clustering method on all inputs, the algorithm should detect nonreal selected eigenpairs and fall back to the already justified symmetric variant.
issues.why_classification: The stated hypotheses admit an explicit counterexample, so the conclusion cannot be recovered by repairing the proof. The key identity is valid only under a strong invariance condition on the fairness subspace, which excludes the advertised general irregular-graph regime. Retraction therefore removes the theorem's central real-spectrum guarantee; a symmetric fallback does not preserve that recorded RW guarantee. Restoring it for general graphs would require a materially redesigned random-walk construction and new analysis, so no established complete route avoids major mathematical loss or essential reconstruction.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Consequently, the reality of its eigenvalues is not theoretically guaranteed in the general case.
